findings.title: Israel says it concludes Gaza tank raid
findings.location: Salah al-Din (Salahudeen) Road, central Gaza Strip
findings.affected_population_system: Road users, displaced civilians and north-south transport access in central Gaza
findings.affected_population: Civilian road users and nearby displaced families; exact number affected by reopening unknown
findings.affected_system: Main north-south Salah al-Din road and security conditions after the incursion
findings.exact_supporting_passage: the main north-south Salahudeen road had been reopened for traffic.
findings.source_type: Established international news reporting attributing Israeli military announcement
findings.summary: Reuters reports that the Israeli military announced completion of its ground/tank operation against a suspected tunnel west of the Yellow Line and said Salah al-Din Road was reopened. Residents separately reported sporadic gunfire and continuing danger; reopening is an Israeli claim, not confirmation the route is safe or fully accessible.

bounded_discovery_context.prior_coverage: November 18 incursion, displacement, road closure and bulldozing already logged; reported termination and claimed reopening are new.
bounded_discovery_context.verification_limits: Military's original Facebook statement not directly obtained; Reuters attributes it. Residents disputed practical safety. Unverified social footage was excluded.

findings.title: Israel says it concludes Gaza tank raid
findings.location: Central Gaza near Nuseirat and Salah al-Din Road
findings.affected_population_system: Palestinian families displaced by the November 18 Israeli incursion
findings.affected_population: Approximately 6,000 people reportedly fled on November 18, according to Gaza government media office; independently verified count unknown
findings.affected_system: Civilian displacement and access to shelter
findings.source_type: Established international news reporting an attributed estimate from Gaza government media office
findings.summary: Reuters supplied a new displacement magnitude: the Gaza government media office estimated about 6,000 people fled the operation area on November 18. This is attributed and not independently confirmed; it does not represent an additional 6,000 beyond previously reported displaced groups, and is not additive to OCHA's population-at-risk figure.

bounded_discovery_context.prior_coverage: Prior watches recorded families/dozens fleeing and an OCHA estimate of 18,000 at risk, not a 6,000-displaced estimate.
bounded_discovery_context.verification_limits: Estimate attributed to Gaza government media office via Reuters; no independent displacement registration or original statement checked. Avoid double counting or converting estimate into verified census.

coverage_notes.purpose: Supplementary humanitarian recall only; primary Gaza collector/publisher remains authoritative.
